newsitem.title: USA: Summers says EMU impasse will not dominate summit.
newsitem.headline: Summers says EMU impasse will not dominate summit.

text.p: U.S. Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers said on Tuesday that he did not believe the upcoming summit of industrial nations in Denver risked being dominated by European turmoil over monetary and currency union.

On Monday, French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn announced at a finance ministers' meeting that his government needed more time to study the so-called stability pact, an integral part of EU plans for economic and monetary union (EMU).
"I'm sure the development will be discussed," Summers told reporters after addressing a trade group here on the June 20-22 Denver summit.

But Summers said he did not expect the topic to become an overriding one. "I think the leaders look forward to a broad-based discussion," which would focus on flexibility and dynamism of economies, he said.
He also told the trade group that he did not fear that the proposed single European currency would be a "threat to the dollar or replace it."
But he said it was important that the debate about a single currency not divert Europe from two key subjects, the unification of Europe and the resurrection of what he called dynamism of economies.
